hypothesis: PySnooper's get_source_from_frame decodes source files using the locale-dependent default encoding when no PEP-263 coding declaration is present, so a UTF-8 source file containing non-ASCII characters is mis-decoded (mojibake) under a non-UTF-8 locale, corrupting the traced source line.
trigger: Create a temporary module file encoded as UTF-8 whose function body contains a non-ASCII string literal (e.g. 'héllo') and no coding declaration; import it, decorate the function with pysnooper.snoop(string_io), and run it under a non-UTF-8 locale (LC_ALL=C).

oracle.expected_behavior: The trace output must contain the exact non-ASCII source line text (e.g. the literal 'héllo') as written in the UTF-8 file, independent of the process locale.
oracle.target_evidence: pysnooper/tracer.py get_source_from_frame: when source is bytes it sets encoding='ascii' and only overrides it if a PEP-263 coding declaration is found in the first two lines; otherwise it decodes with that encoding. The README and tests (e.g. test_unavailable_source, test_string_io) show source lines are echoed verbatim into trace output, so a mis-decoded line is a functional defect.
oracle.historical_evidence: cookiecutter:1 shows the same class of locale-dependent implicit text decoding bug (UTF-8 data read with platform default encoding); PySnooper:3 is only weakly related (file-output path variable mismatch).

preconditions: Python 3.9.18 with LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 so locale.getpreferredencoding(False) is ANSI_X3.4-1968/ascii
A temporary module file is written as UTF-8 bytes with no PEP-263 coding declaration and contains a non-ASCII string literal in a function body
pysnooper is importable from the checkout

initial_state.named_state: temp module file utf8_no_coding.py exists on sys.path containing a snooped function whose body line is: return 'héllo'

actions.description: Set LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 in the subprocess environment before starting Python
Create io.StringIO() named string_io and import the module so the decorator registers the function code
Call module.f() so the tracer executes and get_source_from_frame reads the file bytes
Read string_io.getvalue() and locate the trace line containing 'return'

plans.expected_invariant: The traced source line for the return statement contains the exact literal 'héllo' as written in the UTF-8 file, not replacement characters or mojibake

observable.measurement_point: after module.f() returns, on the captured StringIO trace text
observable.extraction_method: string_io.getvalue() then select the line whose text contains 'return' and inspect the source-line portion

assertion.predicate: the selected trace line contains the substring "héllo"
assertion.failure_condition: the trace line contains 'h\ufffdllo', 'h?llo', or any byte-mangled variant instead of 'héllo'
assertion.rationale: get_source_from_frame decodes file bytes with encoding='ascii' when no coding declaration exists, so under LC_ALL=C the non-ASCII literal is corrupted; the trace echoes source lines verbatim, making the exact literal the direct observable of correct decoding

actions.description: Set LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=0, PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 in the subprocess environment

Write utf8_withblock.py as UTF-8 bytes with no coding declaration: 'import pysnooper
def h(string_io):
    with pysnooper.snoop(string_io):
        value = 'h\xc3\xa9llo'
    return value
'
Create io.StringIO() named string_io and import the module
Call module.h(string_io) so the with-block tracer reads and echoes the non-ASCII source line
Read string_io.getvalue() and select the trace line containing 'value ='

plans.expected_invariant: The traced source line inside the with block contains the exact literal 'héllo' from the UTF-8 file

observable.source: pysnooper.tracer.get_source_from_frame via the pysnooper.snoop() context-manager trace output
observable.measurement_point: after module.h(string_io) returns, on the captured StringIO trace text
observable.extraction_method: string_io.getvalue() then select the line containing 'value =' and inspect its source-line portion

assertion.predicate: the selected trace line contains the substring "héllo"
assertion.failure_condition: the trace line contains replacement characters or mojibake instead of the exact literal
assertion.rationale: the with-block path also calls get_source_from_frame and echoes the source line, so the same locale-dependent ascii decode corrupts the literal; exact literal presence measures correct decoding through a different public interface path
